newsitem.title: UK: British billionaire prepares to bash Euro-union.
newsitem.headline: British billionaire prepares to bash Euro-union.

text.p: Billionaire Sir James Goldsmith said on Friday the inaugural conference of his Referendum Party would expose the erosion of British sovereignty to voters reared on a diet of pro-Europe propaganda.
"This is a major moment in our nation's history -- whether we should continue as an independent nation," said Goldsmith who plans to put forward about 600 candidates at the next election.
"The purpose of our conference is to address the issues so the people are knowledgable of the realities and not the propaganda," he told reporters.
Goldsmith, who amassed a fortune as an entrepeneur, wants a referendum on Britain's future in Europe and says he will dissolve his Euro-party once this objective is achieved.
The conference, taking place in a southcoast resort facing France, will be attended by 4,200 delegates and 187 candidates already selected to fight the election.

Conservative Prime Minister John Major's pledge to hold a referendum after the election, due by May, on whether Britain should join a European single currency if parliament had decided in favour, is dismissed by Goldsmith as too little too late.
Goldsmith claims increasing support from traditional Conservative voters fearful of European federalism and the influence of Brussels in British life.

But Major said on Friday he did not believe the referendum group would damage his party, already more than 20 points behind opposition Labour in opinion polls. "I don't believe they will get very many votes. They are very much a fringe organisation," Major said.

Goldsmith, swamped by journalists on his arrival, dismissed the notion he was playing political games with his vast fortune. "We are not a fringe party. It's not for him (Major) to decide, it's for the people to decide."
"The purpose of the conference is substance rather than form. Over the past four years the realities that are actually taking place (over Europe) have been hidden on purpose from the British people."
It is still unclear whether Goldsmith, who closes the conference with a speech on Saturday, would like Britain to withdraw from the European Union or just step aside from further integration.

In the run-up to the one-day conference Goldsmith has been running full-page advertisements in broadsheet newspapers under the heading "The First Referendum Party Confernce. The Last Chance for Britain?"
Over the past few weeks, several well-known figures including former Conservative Party treasurer Lord McAlpine and actor Edward Fox have joined the party's ranks.

Fox, star of the film "Day of the Jackal", will give a speech on "Why referenda are part of the British tradition" but the actor's views on Europe have given weight to accusations Goldsmith's party has xenophobic leanings.
In a newspaper article on Sunday, Fox said he believed Goldsmith could be the Winston Churchill of the hour and he warned of appeasement towards Europe.
"We should be very careful about the psychology of Germany. Just as (World War Two leader) Churchill made that stand against Germany in the last war, we need someone to do the same now," Fox said.
